maya: Heads-up — we got a community-submitted model bundle for onboarding. Contains weights + tokenizer + a small conversion script. Need to ingest into the model registry with full provenance checks before any evals. Who can own the artifact verification and registry handoff?

sahil: I can own verification (checksums + signatures). @maya can you paste the S3 path? :+1:

maya: s3://redwood-incoming/models/mpt-lite-community/2026-03-18/upload.tar.gz uploaded by third-party-bot. Bot claimed sha256: 3f8b2c... (short).

artifact-bot: New artifact uploaded by third-party-bot:
```
name: mpt-lite-community
path: s3://redwood-incoming/models/mpt-lite-community/2026-03-18/upload.tar.gz
files: [weights.bin, tokenizer.json, convert.py, model_card.md]
claimed_sha256: 3f8b2c1d4a5e6f7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b
uploader: third-party-bot
```

ben: I'll take tokenizer sanity checks and a quick generation smoke test. Typical steps: load tokenizer, run tokenization on a couple prompts, check vocab size + special tokens.

lena: Also need a legal/license check and provenance metadata in the registry entry: origin_url, source_commit (if available), uploader identity, license text or SPDX, conversion steps, tool versions (transformers/convert script sha), and a statement whether weights were fine-tuned vs. pretraining checkpoint. I'll sketch a mandatory metadata schema below.

ben: Quick tokenizer test snippet I use:
```
python - <<PY
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('local/path/to/tokenizer')
print('vocab_size=', tok.vocab_size)
print('special_tokens=', tok.all_special_tokens)
print(tok('Hello world'))
PY
```

maya: Good. @sahil what exact commands do you want run for checksum/signature verification?

sahil: Steps I recommend:
1) Download artifact to isolated host.
2) Verify sha256 locally: `sha256sum upload.tar.gz` and match claimed value.
3) If we get a detached signature file (.sig) verify with GPG: `gpg --keyring /opt/keys/trusted.gpg --verify upload.tar.gz.sig upload.tar.gz` (we maintain a fingerprint allowlist).
4) Compute per-file checksums after extraction and store them in the registry as `artifact.files[*].sha256`.

Example commands:
```
sha256sum upload.tar.gz
tar -xzvf upload.tar.gz
sha256sum weights.bin tokenizer.json convert.py
```

sahil: If any checksum mismatch, quarantine the upload and open an incident channel.

lena: Registry metadata (proposed required fields):
- model_id (string)
- version (string)
- origin_url (string)
- source_commit (string)
- uploader (string)
- claimed_sha256 (string)
- files: list of {name, path, sha256, size_bytes, role}
- license (string, SPDX)
- conversion_steps (string)
- tool_versions (string)
- provenance_notes (string)
- verification_status (enum: pending/verified/failed)
- related_artifacts (list)  # e.g., quantized variants, eval results

ben: For weights validation: load a tiny forward pass to check shapes + no runtime errors. Example run (pseudo):
```
from transformers import AutoModel
m = AutoModel.from_pretrained('local/path/to/weights')
# run a single forward with random input to catch shape mismatches
```
If that passes, run a short per-layer param-sum sanity check (compare against expected ranges).

maya: About storage/naming — we should separate raw upstream artifacts vs. registry canonical copies. Proposal:
- Raw incoming: s3://redwood-incoming/<model>-<date>/upload.tar.gz
- Canonical registry store: s3://redwood-models/<model_id>/versions/<semver>/artifacts/<artifact-hash>/weights.bin
- Quantized/experiment outputs: s3://redwood-models/<model_id>/experiments/<exp-id>/artifacts/

sahil: Naming convention: artifact-hash = sha256 of tarball. Registry must store mapping: version -> canonical artifact-hash -> file entries. Use tags: `artifact:raw`, `artifact:canonical`, `artifact:quantized`.

maya: Quantization experiments — should we create new registry entries for each quantized variant? I want a traceable parent-child link.

lena: Yes. Each quantized artifact must have `provenance.parent_artifact` pointing to canonical weights, plus fields: quantization_method, bit_width, calibration_dataset, recipe_hash, quant_tool_version. Also save test_results_url that has accuracy/latency/regression flags.

ben: For experiments, we should also snapshot the prompt/eval set used for quality checks and store a small eval report (json or markdown) under the related_artifacts list.

maya: OK plan of action:
- @sahil verify checksums and signatures, produce per-file sha256 and update registry entry.
- @ben run tokenizer + forward-pass smoke tests and produce a short report (attach to registry).
- @lena do license/provenance metadata and file the registry record skeleton.
- I'll open a PR to the registry schema to add the fields discussed and create the canonical storage path, then assign tasks.

sahil: Got it, I'll start the verification run now. Will post logs here and a JSON with file checksums when done. :white_check_mark:

ben: Starting tokenizer checks in a few mins. Will attach a small sample output.

lena: I'll draft the registry record now and ping legal if license text looks weird.

maya: Thanks team. If anything fails, tag #eng-ml and #incidents depending on severity. :rocket:
